###Part A
```{r}
m <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)
 
 apply(m, 1, sum)
 apply(m, 2, sum)
 class(lapply(1:3, function(i) i^2))
 sapply(1:3, function(i) i^2)
 sapply(c('a', 'bb', 'ccc'), nchar)
 mapply(function(x, y) x * y, 1:3, 4:6)
 tapply(c(10, 20, 30, 40), c('u', 'v', 'u', 'v'), sum)
```


###Part B.1
```{r}
scores <- matrix(c(70, 85, 90,
                   60, 75, 80,
                   88, 92, 79),
                 nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE,
                 dimnames = list(c('Ana', 'Ben', 'Cara'), c('Math', 'Sci', 'Eng')))
 
temps <- list(Mon = c(30, 32, 31), Tue = c(29, 33), Wed = c(31, 34, 35, 30))

avg <- apply(scores, MARGIN = 1, FUN = mean)
max <- apply(scores, MARGIN = 2, FUN = max)
subject <- apply(scores, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x) colnames(scores)[which.max(x)])
avg
max
subject


```

###Part B.2
```{r}
daily_mean <- lapply(temps, mean)
daily_mean
daily_count <- vapply(temps, length, FUN.VALUE = integer(1))
daily_count
daily_range <- sapply(temps, range)
daily_range
```

```{r}
sapply(list(a = 1:3, b = 4:6), mean)
### mean() calls the function immediately instead of passing into sapply()
apply(matrix(1:6, nrow = 3), 2, mean)
### Margin = 1 applies mean in rows instead of columns
df <- data.frame(n = c(1, 2), s = c('a', 'b'))
sapply(df, class)
### apply() first turns the data frame into a matrix, converting all numbers into text so every column reports "character" instead of its original class
```
